ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is quadrilateral JFGH, with vertex J at the lower left, F at the upper left, G at the upper right, and H at the lower right; two diagonals JG and FH are drawn, and they intersect at point K. Reasoning: If quadrilateral JFGH is a parallelogram, then the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so K is the midpoint of diagonal FH. Therefore FK = KH. Given FK = 3x - 1 and KH = 2x + 3, set up the equation 3x - 1 = 2x + 3, solving gives x = 4.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as quadrilateral JFGH with diagonals FH and JG intersecting at K. From the text, use the given segment lengths FK = 3x - 1 and KH = 2x + 3. Since the quadrilateral is required to be a parallelogram, apply the theorem that diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so K is the midpoint of diagonal FH. Therefore FK = KH, giving 3x - 1 = 2x + 3, hence x = 4.
